questions.q: Which DOC covers the whole of Sardinia for the island's signature red grape, Grenache under its local name?
questions.exp: Cannonau di Sardegna DOC (1972) covers the whole island and asks at least 85 per cent Cannonau, with the Classico, Jerzu, Oliena and Capo Ferrato sub-zones; Carignano del Sulcis is the south west's Carignan, Monica di Sardegna another island wide red, and Vermentino di Gallura the white DOCG.

questions.q: Since the 2017 vintage a varietal Grillo or Nero d'Avola may no longer be sold as Terre Siciliane IGT. Which island wide DOC must it carry instead, unless a smaller DOC applies?
questions.exp: Sicilia DOC, the Court's Sicily DOC, was created in 2011 to replace the island wide IGT and has held varietal Grillo and Nero d'Avola to itself since the 2017 vintage, with Terre Siciliane IGT left beneath it for everything else.

questions.q: Which sea lies between Sardinia and the Italian mainland, washing Sicily's northern coast as well?
questions.exp: The Tyrrhenian Sea fills the basin between Sardinia, Corsica, Sicily and the west coast of the mainland, and the Court names it with Etna as the islands' physical features; Sicily's east coast faces the Ionian instead.

questions.q: Which white grape must make up at least 60 per cent of an Etna Bianco?
questions.exp: Carricante, the Court's Sicilian white, makes at least 60 per cent of Etna Bianco and 80 per cent of the Bianco Superiore from Milo; it ripens late on the volcano's eastern slopes and keeps high acidity with a saline, citrus edge.

questions.q: Grillo and Catarratto share the blend of a golden Marsala with which third white grape the Court names?
questions.exp: Inzolia, called Ansonica on the mainland, is a soft, nutty white that joins Grillo and Catarratto in Oro and Ambra Marsala and in dry western blends; Carricante belongs to Etna, Zibibbo to Pantelleria and Vermentino to Sardinia.

questions.q: Sardinia lies directly south of which island, across the narrow Strait of Bonifacio?
questions.exp: Corsica, which is French, lies across the Strait of Bonifacio from Sardinia's north coast, which is why the Court places Sardinia south of France and west of Italy; Elba and Capraia are Tuscan islands and Menorca is one of Spain's Balearics.

questions.q: Marsala is labelled by its sugar in three levels the Court names. Between Secco and Dolce, which word marks the middle one?
questions.exp: Marsala's sweetness words run Secco, Semi-Secco and Dolce, the Court's label terms, and they apply to the Fine and Superiore grades; Vergine takes no sweetening at all and is always dry.
